body:
## Problem

A `--listen` path longer than the system socket path limit (about 104 bytes on macOS, 108 on Linux) is silently truncated by `uv_pipe_bind()`. Nvim either serves a socket at a different path than `v:servername` reports, or fails with an error that blames the full untruncated path:

    nvim: Failed to --listen: address already in use: "<full path>"

## Solution

Bind with `uv_pipe_bind2()` and `UV_PIPE_NO_TRUNCATE` (libuv 1.46+), so a too-long path fails up front with the actual reason:

    nvim: Failed to --listen: invalid argument: "<full path>"

Older libuv falls back to `uv_pipe_bind()`, same as the version guard in `event/stream.c`. `uv_pipe_connect()` has the same latent truncation, left alone here to keep this focused on the reported problem.

Extends the "startup --listen validates" test. Without the fix it fails: nvim exits 0 after binding the truncated path. The new case is gated on libuv 1.46+, since older libuv keeps the truncating fallback.

Fixes #38623

would like to merge this, but 2 tests are failing. this one looks like an easy update:

fixed both. they were failing because NO_TRUNCATE also affects the autogenerated server address, not just `--listen`. 962 drops `--listen`, so with a deep `TMPDIR` and no `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` the generated socket runs past `sun_path` and fails to bind now (gave that test a short `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`).
so the default server errors now instead of truncating when the runtime dir is too long. i think that's fine, it's basically #30282 already, but if you'd rather keep the old default-server behavior i can scope NO_TRUNCATE to user-supplied addresses only.

makes sense. though digging in a bit, `find_package(Libuv 1.28.0)` doesn't actually enforce the version right now (FindLibuv.cmake never reads uv/version.h), so requiring 1.46 means teaching FindLibuv to parse it, on top of dropping the shim. it'd also drop system libuv <1.46, which a few LTS distros still ship. could do that as its own PR to keep this one a plain bugfix (and drop the stale stream.c shim while i'm there), or fold it in here. whichever works.

> drop system libuv <1.46, which a few LTS distros still ship.

those distros will fail to build because UV_PIPE_NO_TRUNCATE is not defined there.

i will update the `find_package` separately. it does enforce version.

i bumped our libuv minimum: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40648

sooo can we wrap this up
done, shim's gone. also dropped the now-redundant `vim.uv.version()` guard in the test since 1.46 is the floor.

Here's AI-generated explanation, but it makes sense:
<details>
it's path length, and now I can show the exact chain rather than assert it.

  What actually gets bound. The harness passes --listen "T160". In server_start(), an address with no / or : is treated as a name, so it's expanded by
  server_address_new():

  // non-Windows branch of server_address_new()
  char *dir = stdpaths_get_xdg_var(kXDGRuntimeDir);          // $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR …
  snprintf(fmt, ..., "%s/%s.%" PRIu64 ".%" PRIu32,
           dir, name, os_get_pid(), count++);                // → "<dir>/T160.<pid>.<count>"

  So the real socket path is <runtime_dir>/T160.<pid>.<count>, not the short "T160" you see in the error.

  Where <runtime_dir> comes from in the Nix sandbox. $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset during the build, so stdpaths.c falls back:

  } else if (idx == kXDGRuntimeDir) {
      ret = vim_gettempdir();     // a dir under $TMPDIR

  and $TMPDIR in the Nix build sandbox is a long path (/private/tmp/nix-build-neovim-unwrapped-7dccbfe.drv-0/… / a vim_mktempdir subdir under it). Prefix that long dir to
  /T160.<pid>.<count> and you blow past the socket limit.

  Why macOS specifically. The AF_UNIX address limit is a hard, OS-defined size of the sun_path field in struct sockaddr_un:
  - macOS/BSD: 104 bytes
  - Linux: 108 bytes

  The expanded path lands in that 104–108 window: it fits on Linux, overflows on macOS. That 4-byte difference is the entire reason it's aarch64-darwin-only.

  Why it only broke now. Before PR #40625:

  uv_pipe_bind(&handle, addr);                                  // silently truncates over-limit paths

  libuv memcpy-truncated the over-length path and returned success — the test limped along (both the child that binds and the harness that connects derive the same
  truncated path, so RPC still connected). After #40625:

  uv_pipe_bind2(&handle, addr, strlen(addr), UV_PIPE_NO_TRUNCATE);  // over-limit → EINVAL

  UV_PIPE_NO_TRUNCATE makes libuv reject the over-length path up front with EINVAL, so every child nvim aborts before serving → EOF was received from Nvim → the whole
  functionaltest checkPhase fails.

  And the misleading "T160" in the message is a known artifact (neovim #38623): the error prints the original listen_addr argument, not the expanded over-length path that
  actually failed:

  "Failed to --listen: %s: \"%s\"", os_strerror(rv), listen_addr   // listen_addr == "T160"

  So: correct on all counts — it's a length overflow of the expanded Unix-socket path against macOS's 104-byte sun_path, turned from a silent no-op into a hard failure by
  #40625. The underlying bug is neovim's own functionaltest harness using name-style --listen addresses that expand under a long $TMPDIR — which is exactly what a Nix
  darwin build provides.
</details>

> TMPDIR in the Nix build sandbox is a long path (/private/tmp/nix-build-neovim-unwrapped-7dccbfe.drv-0/… / 

@konradmalik can you give an example of a full `stdpath('run')` path on your system?

yeah, this is a "normal" non-sandboxed path used when using macOS:
```
/var/folders/4h/9rqxkp99717gsl11d3nx80qh0000gn/T/
```

and this is when running inside nix-sandbox for neovim functionaltest (where apparently XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset and stdpath('run') falls back to tmpdir if I get this correctly):
```
/private/tmp/nix-build-neovim-unwrapped-7dccbfe.drv-0/source/build/Xtest_xdg/nvim.konrad/HRmg49
```

If XDG_RUNTIME_DIR was defined in the sandbox, it would result in something like:
```
/nix/var/nix/builds/nix-26432-585754608/nvim._nixbld1/OHRhc0
```
wtf are apps supposed to do when OSes just vomit out such long /tmp paths, and the max socket length is 100 chars?
🥲 not sure, maybe this should be patched in neovim derivation in nixpkgs instead
